chunks.question: How much annual leave does a full-time employee receive?
chunks.answer: A full-time employee receives 20 working days of paid annual leave per calendar year. Employees who join during the year and part-time employees receive a prorated entitlement based on their start date or contracted schedule. The People Operations portal displays each employee's current balance. A leave request is not approved until the reporting manager confirms it in the portal.

chunks.question: How do I request annual leave, and how much notice is needed?
chunks.answer: Submit an annual leave request in the People Operations portal at least five working days before the intended start date. The reporting manager checks team coverage and either approves or declines the request in the portal. Do not treat a submitted request as approval. If a genuine emergency prevents five working days of notice, contact the manager directly and record the request as soon as practicable.

chunks.question: What is the sick leave allowance and when is a medical certificate required?
chunks.answer: Eligible full-time employees may use up to 10 paid sick days per calendar year. Notify the reporting manager and record the absence in the People Operations portal by 9:30 a.m. local time on the first day, when reasonably possible. A medical certificate is required for an absence lasting more than two consecutive working days. People Operations can advise on statutory entitlements where local rules differ.

chunks.question: Can unused annual leave be carried into the next year?
chunks.answer: With reporting-manager approval, an employee may carry forward up to five unused annual leave days. Approved carryover must be used by 31 March of the following calendar year; any remainder expires unless applicable law requires otherwise. The People Operations team records approved carryover in the portal. Unused leave is not automatically paid out during employment.

chunks.question: What should I do if an urgent personal situation prevents me from working?
chunks.answer: Contact your reporting manager as soon as it is safe to do so and explain the expected period of absence. The manager and People Operations will determine whether annual leave, sick leave, unpaid leave, or an applicable statutory category should be used. An urgent absence can be reported before its category is finalized, but the employee must update the People Operations portal when the appropriate category is confirmed.

chunks.question: Which public holiday calendar applies to remote and hybrid employees?
chunks.answer: The published holiday calendar for the employee's assigned office location normally applies, including when the employee is working remotely within the same country. Working temporarily from another location does not automatically change the assigned holiday calendar. Employees should consult People Operations before assuming that a holiday in a travel destination replaces a holiday at their assigned office. Any mandatory local-law exception takes precedence.

chunks.question: What are the normal working hours and core collaboration hours?
chunks.answer: The standard full-time schedule is 40 hours per week, ordinarily Monday through Friday, subject to the employment agreement and local requirements. Teams observe core collaboration hours from 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. in the employee's assigned office time zone. Managers may coordinate different arrangements for client coverage or accessibility needs. Core hours are a collaboration window, not an instruction to work without breaks.

chunks.answer: An employee in a role approved for hybrid working may ordinarily work remotely up to two days per week, with the reporting manager's agreement and subject to operational needs. Remote days must be visible on the team calendar. This arrangement is not automatic for roles requiring onsite facilities or customer coverage. Managers may agree temporary changes, but any ongoing change should be documented with People Operations.

chunks.question: Can I work remotely from another country during personal travel?
chunks.answer: Do not work from another country without written approval obtained in advance from both People Operations and Information Security. A manager's informal agreement alone is insufficient because cross-border work may affect employment, tax, security, and data-access obligations. Submit the proposed country, dates, and work activities before departure. Approval may include conditions or may be declined; silence is not approval.

If the absence relates to illness, the sick-leave rules also apply, including the medical certificate requirement for more than two consecutive working days. Eligibility for payment or time off in lieu depends on the employee's contract and applicable local law. Merely remaining online after core hours does not by itself create an approved overtime claim.

chunks.question: What should I do if my internet connection fails while working remotely?
chunks.answer: Notify the reporting manager through an available approved channel as soon as practical, ideally within 30 minutes of identifying a prolonged outage. Attempt a secure alternative such as a company-approved mobile hotspot. Do not use an unsecured shared computer or disable security controls to remain online. If productive work cannot continue, agree on an alternate location, task, or leave arrangement and record any schedule change.

chunks.question: How is an account created for a new employee?
chunks.answer: The hiring manager submits the onboarding access form at least three working days before the employee's start date. The request identifies the role, start date, and approved systems needed for the role. IT provisions a named account after verifying manager authorization. Shared credentials are not issued as a substitute for onboarding. Requests for sensitive systems may require an additional data-owner approval.

chunks.question: Is multi-factor authentication required for company accounts?
chunks.answer: Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for company accounts that support it. Employees should enroll a company-approved authenticator application or security key during onboarding. SMS-based verification is reserved for an IT-approved recovery situation and should not be the normal method. Never approve an unexpected authentication prompt. If a prompt appears without a login attempt, deny it and contact the Service Desk.

chunks.question: How should I reset a forgotten password?
chunks.answer: Use the company self-service password reset page from a trusted device. If the recovery method is unavailable, contact the Service Desk for identity verification before any reset is performed. Do not send passwords or recovery codes by email or chat, and do not ask a colleague to sign in on your behalf. After restoring access, review recent authentication prompts and report anything unfamiliar.

chunks.question: What should I do after receiving a suspicious email?
chunks.answer: Do not click links, open unexpected attachments, or reply with credentials. Report the message using the phishing-report button or forward it as an attachment to security@cedarbridge.example. If a link was clicked or information was entered, contact the Service Desk immediately and explain what happened. Do not delete the email until the security team has advised whether it is needed for investigation.

chunks.question: How quickly must a missing company laptop or phone be reported?
chunks.answer: Report a lost or stolen company device to the Service Desk and Information Security within one hour of discovering the loss, whenever safely possible. Provide the device type, asset tag if known, last known location, and approximate time of loss. IT may suspend sessions or remotely protect managed data. Do not attempt to recover a stolen device through unsafe personal action.

The traveler should choose a safe, reasonably priced option within this ceiling. Any higher rate must receive written manager and Finance approval before booking, unless an emergency makes prior approval impossible. Room upgrades and personal minibar charges are not reimbursable.

chunks.question: What information classification levels does the company use?

The data owner is responsible for assigning an appropriate classification when information is created or significantly changed.

chunks.question: Where should employee or customer personal information be stored?

Retain data only for the approved retention period applicable to the record type. If the correct location or retention rule is unclear, ask the data owner or Privacy team before creating another copy.

Deletion or archival must follow approved procedures, particularly where a legal hold or audit requirement applies. Ask Records Management if the schedule is unclear.

Deletion or archival must follow approved procedures, particularly where a legal hold or audit requirement applies. Ask Records Management if the schedule is unclear.
